### Analysis of Circuit in Figure Q.4
The circuit is a **negative clamper** with a negative DC reference voltage source of $10\text{ V}$ in series with a diode and parallel to resistor $R$.

* **Input Voltage ($v_i$):** Sinusoidal wave with peak values $+20\text{ V}$ and $-20\text{ V}$.
* **Diode State:** The diode points upwards with a $-10\text{ V}$ source in its branch. 

During the negative half-cycle of $v_i$, the capacitor charges up. The total voltage level shifted is determined by the DC source and peak input voltage:
* Maximum positive peak of output: $V_{omax} = V_{i(peak)} + V_{i(peak)} - V_{bias} = 20 + 20 - 10 = 30\text{ V}$ (depending on exact clamping level).
* Because of the $-10\text{ V}$ battery opposing/shifting the level, the lower level of the waveform is clamped at $-10\text{ V}$.

### Output Waveform Summary
* **Lower clamping level:** $-10\text{ V}$
* **Peak-to-peak amplitude:** Remains $40\text{ V}$ ($+30\text{ V}$ to $-10\text{ V}$).
proTip: In clamper circuits, the peak-to-peak value of the output waveform always equals the peak-to-peak value of the input sinusoidal signal.
